title: Capital Stops in the Northeast
description: Visit state capitals from New England to the Mid-Atlantic, with a few map and civic words to help the crossings.
cardDescription: Visit state capitals from New England to the Mid-Atlantic, with a few map and civic words to help the crossings.
focus: Most clues name a state and ask for its capital. These are state seats of government, which need not be the largest or best-known city in the state.
solvingTip: Start with a capital you recognize, then use crossing letters for a less familiar city. Hints remain available for place names.
words: Building where a state legislature meets
Drawing used to locate these northeastern cities
One of the fifty US political units whose capitals are clued
Government center, in the phrase county or state ___

answerNotes.BOSTON: Boston is the capital of Massachusetts. The clue asks for a city, not the state's name.
answerNotes.ALBANY: Albany is New York State's capital. New York City is larger but is not the state capital.
answerNotes.AUGUSTA: Augusta is Maine's capital. Portland is another Maine city, but it is not the seat of state government.
answerNotes.CONCORD: Concord is the capital of New Hampshire. Its spelling is the same as an ordinary word meaning agreement.
answerNotes.CAPITOL: Capitol with an o names the legislative building. Capital with an a names the city in the geography clues.

title: Capital Stops in the Southeast
description: Trace southeastern state capitals and practice distinguishing a capital city from a government building.
cardDescription: Trace southeastern state capitals and practice distinguishing a capital city from a government building.
focus: The state names provide the main hints. A few short civic and direction words give entry points around the longer city names.
solvingTip: Read each state name carefully. A familiar city from the same state may be a tempting answer, but the clue asks for the capital.
words: City serving as the seat of a state's government
Compass direction suggested by this southeastern region
Type of place named by a state-capital answer
Relating to a city or its public affairs

answerNotes.ATLANTA: Atlanta is Georgia's capital. A state-capital clue asks where the state government is based.
answerNotes.RALEIGH: Raleigh is North Carolina's capital. Charlotte is a different North Carolina city, not the state capital.
answerNotes.COLUMBIA: Columbia is the capital of South Carolina. It should not be confused with Columbus, which is Ohio's capital.
answerNotes.RICHMOND: Richmond is Virginia's capital. The city named by a state clue is different from the federal capital, Washington, DC.
answerNotes.CAPITAL: Capital ends in al and names a city in these clues. Capitol ends in ol and names a legislature's building.

title: Capital Stops in the Midwest
description: Cross the Midwest through state-capital clues, including several cities that are easily confused with larger neighbors.
cardDescription: Cross the Midwest through state-capital clues, including several cities that are easily confused with larger neighbors.
focus: These clues name capital cities in the Midwest and central United States. Long place names have direct state clues, and shorter regional words can help you enter the board.
solvingTip: Use the number of squares to check a long city name. Spaces in multiword answers are omitted from the grid.
words: State capital of Iowa, with spaces omitted
State capital of Minnesota, with spaces omitted
Broad grassland associated with parts of the central United States
Large area of relatively level land
Middle location, as suggested by the central states
Direction opposite south on a Midwest road map
Compass direction opposite west on a central-state map
Inland body of water shown on a regional map
Solid surface represented by most of a state map
Mark separating state areas on a map

answerNotes.LANSING: Lansing is Michigan's capital. Detroit is larger but is not the state capital.
answerNotes.MADISON: Madison is Wisconsin's capital. The familiar city name Milwaukee answers a different location question.
answerNotes.COLUMBUS: Columbus is Ohio's capital. Its final us distinguishes it from Columbia, South Carolina's capital.
answerNotes.DESMOINES: Des Moines is written as two words in ordinary text. The crossword places DESMOINES in one uninterrupted run of squares.
answerNotes.BISMARCK: Bismarck is North Dakota's capital. Fargo is a different city in the state.

title: Capital Stops from the Gulf to the Rockies
description: Explore state capitals from the Gulf states toward the Rocky Mountains, with river and map words to help the crossings.
cardDescription: Explore state capitals from the Gulf states toward the Rocky Mountains, with river and map words to help the crossings.
subtheme: Capital Stops from the Gulf to the Rockies
focus: This puzzle groups Gulf-state, south-central, and Rocky Mountain capitals for a word-game route. The state names in the clues identify the cities; it is not an official regional classification.
solvingTip: Do not assume that the most famous city is the capital. For a two-word city, write the letters together without a blank square.
words: State capital of Louisiana, with spaces omitted
State capital of Arkansas, with spaces omitted
State capital of New Mexico, with spaces omitted
First word of Missouri's capital, ___ City
State-name word completing ___ City, the Sooner State's capital
Flowing waterway that can pass through a capital city
Surface route linking stops on a capital-city trip
Book containing maps for locating these cities
Area grouped by location or shared features

answerNotes.AUSTIN: Austin is Texas's capital. Houston and Dallas are larger cities, but neither is the state capital.
answerNotes.BATONROUGE: Baton Rouge is Louisiana's capital. New Orleans is a different Louisiana city; the two words of Baton Rouge run together in the grid.
answerNotes.JACKSON: Jackson is Mississippi's capital. The direct state name in the clue identifies which place named Jackson is intended.
answerNotes.LITTLEROCK: Little Rock is written as two words outside the puzzle. The answer uses all ten letters without a space.
answerNotes.INDIANA: Indiana is the state; Indianapolis is its capital. The clue deliberately asks for the state name, which fits a shorter answer.

title: Capital Stops in the West
description: Head west through capital-city clues, with map directions and landscape words to open the crossings.
cardDescription: Head west through capital-city clues, with map directions and landscape words to open the crossings.
focus: These place clues cover western states, including Alaska and Hawaii. A two-word capital is entered without spaces when the clue says so, and short direction and landscape words help with crossings.
solvingTip: A city famous for tourism or business is not always the capital. Check the state clue and the answer length before entering it.
words: Nevada capital beginning with C, two words
First two words of Utah's capital, ___ City
Direction opposite east on a map of these states
Ocean bordering the US West Coast
Land bordering an ocean along the western states

answerNotes.SALEM: Salem is Oregon's capital. Portland is a larger Oregon city but is not the state capital.
answerNotes.OLYMPIA: Olympia is Washington State's capital. Washington, DC is the federal capital and is a different place.
answerNotes.SACRAMENTO: Sacramento is California's capital. Neither Los Angeles nor San Francisco is the state capital.
answerNotes.PHOENIX: Phoenix is the capital of Arizona. The same spelling also names a legendary bird, but the clue here is geographic.
answerNotes.HONOLULU: Honolulu is Hawaii's capital, on the island of Oahu. The answer names a city rather than the island or the state.
